newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shrs end off as foreign buyers steer clear.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shrs end off as foreign buyers steer clear.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed lower in slow trade as foreign investors shunned the market awaiting clarification of how recent policy developments would affect the market, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 1.65 percent to 6,278.51 as 25 stocks fell, five rose and eight closed flat.
A historic agreement signed Monday to reform the severance payments system had not affected the market, brokers said.
"Foreign investors are waiting to see how it plays out," said Miguel Ortiz of the Financorp brokerage.
"The market was only used by locals; it was very slow and weak," another broker said. Markets are closed Wednesday for the San Jose market holiday.
The composite Merinvest index also closed lower, slipping 1.60 percent to 97.02. A total of 1.407 billion bolivars ($2.9 million) changed hands in 514 trades.

Among heavily traded stocks, Electricidad de Caracas fell 7.00 bolivars to 514.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa fell 5.00 bolivars to 145.00 bolivars and telephone company CANTV slipped 29.00 bolivars to 2,071.00 bolivars.
